title: two Eids, not one
hookLine: new clothes, an envelope from an uncle, and the second Eid people forget
tomorrow: the greeting that is a wish
last: BISMILLAH · AL-FATIHA · WUDU · INSHALLAH · IMAN · RAMADAN

cards: The morning after Ramadan ends, kids are up early in new clothes. An uncle hands out envelopes of money.
The family heads to a prayer held in the morning, and then it's visits, sweets, and Eid Mubarak said so many times it blurs.
And yet plenty of people, Muslims included, half forget there's a second Eid a couple of months later, or what makes it different. Today, both.

teach.h: EID — A DAY THAT COMES BACK AROUND.
teach.b: Eid is tied to a root meaning to return: a day that comes back around, every year. When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrived in Medina, a saying reports, people there had two old days of games and celebration.
God has given you two better ones, he told them: the day of breaking the fast, and the day of sacrifice. The first is Eid al-Fitr.
Fitr means breaking the fast. It closes Ramadan, and before the Eid prayer, each household gives a small gift of food, zakat al-fitr, so people in need can celebrate too.

teach.h: EID AL-ADHA — THE FEAST OF SACRIFICE.
teach.b: The second is Eid al-Adha, the feast of sacrifice. It falls during the hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, and it remembers Ibrahim, Abraham, and the ram given in place of his son.
Families who are able offer an animal, and share the meat with relatives, neighbors and people in need. So one Eid closes a month of fasting, and the other comes with the pilgrimage.

teach.h: NOBODY LEFT OUT OF THE FEAST.
teach.b: Both begin with a prayer, and both are built so nobody is left out of the feast. And Eid Mubarak? A blessed Eid.

how: On both Eids Muslims gather in the morning for the Eid prayer, dress in their best, visit family, share food and greet each other with Eid Mubarak; children often get gifts of money. Before Eid al-Fitr each household gives zakat al-fitr, and at Eid al-Adha those able offer an animal and share the meat.

games.q: the Prophet ﷺ arrives in Medina and finds people keeping two old days of games every year. what does he tell them?
o: give them up and keep no feast at all.
God has given you two better days.
keep them just as they are.
games.why: two better days: the day of breaking the fast and the day of sacrifice. the two Eids.

games.q: build the name: feast + breaking the fast.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, picture a table set for a feast. On the second, picture who's around it: your people.
On the third, add one more chair, for someone who might not have a table of their own today.
